newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices soar ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices soar ahead of weekend.

text.p: Fueled by a rising heating demand and a reluctance to tap into storage inventories, U.S. spot natgas prices moved significantly higher Friday, industry sources said.

Gulf Coast gas prices soared into the low-$2 to $2.20 range, with most trades reported done in the $2.10-2.12 area. Transco (Station 65) led the market higher early with gas selling as high as $2.20 for the weekend.
The south Texas market was equally stronger in the $2.01-2.08 range, with further support coming from the firm Permian basin market.
Contrary to what most traders had expected ahead of the weekend, prices in the Permian basin gained another five or six cents today to about the $1.90 area.
Similarly at the southern California border, prices were up about 10 cents to the low-$2 area.
Some sources speculated that buyers may be replenishing storage inventories following last week's cold spell in western Canada, which limited Alberta supplies to the West Coast.

In the Midcontinent, prices rose by about one to two cents to the $1.85-1.90 range despite milder temperatures in the region. Most sources attributed the firmness to low storage levels and buyers' reluctance to further deplete them ahead of the winter.

Prices held for the weekend, but forecasts for milder temperatures beginning Sunday in the Northeast may result in some downward pressure on the market early next week, traders said. The interest in storage injections will be the key factor.
